newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Crown denies project cost overruns.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Crown denies project cost overruns.

text.p: Australian casino operator Crown Ltd denied on Friday its new casino, hotel and shopping complex in Melbourne had run into cost overruns.
Crown, due in April to move into its permanent premises beside the city's Yarra River, was responding to media reports that the project cost had ballooned and could top A$2 billion.
Crown shares have fallen over 20 percent since mid-January. The slide continued on Friday morning, with the shares trading six cents lower than Thursday's close at A$2.10 at 2325 GMT (10.25 a.m.).
Investors were also reported to have been disappointed by Crown's announcement on Thursday of a A$185 million one-for-six rights issue to refinance its secured debt facility.

The rights issue follows two share placements in December and January to raise A$124.38 million and comes ahead of the expiry of options over 74.5 million new shares in the company by major shareholder Hudson Conway Ltd.
Crown also announced on Thursday it estimated the total capital cost of the project at A$1.55 billion, up from an earlier estimate of A$1.25 billion at the end of December.
The estimates did not include the cost of a planned second hotel tower and lyric theatre at the site. This had been separately estimated to cost A$150 million, Crown said.

"The project is coming towards completion. There's obviously been additional expenditure on plant, property and equipment but we are fairly happy with that level of expenditure," Crown spokesman Gary O'Neill told Reuters.
He referred to one newspaper report that the total capital cost, including the second tower, could hit A$2.2 billion.
"I am mystified as to why they are claiming such a cost overrun," O'Neill said.
On top of the capital costs of the project, Crown was also negotiating to buy the management rights to the operation from Hudson Conway, which is estimated to cost up to A$300 million.
Crown was also reported to be interested in acquiring a golf course for use by its high-rolling patrons for A$40 miillion.
